title: PossibleCooker Mushroom Barley with Hazelnut Butter
description: Quick barley simmers in mushroom broth and finishes with browned butter and smooth hazelnut paste for a soft, savory side.

ingredients.name: quick-cooking pearl barley
ingredients.note: Choose a variety labeled for about 10 minutes.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: Use plain mushroom broth made with mushrooms and water.

ingredients.name: smooth unsalted hazelnut paste
ingredients.note: Pure hazelnuts with no coarse pieces or added sugar.

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: Keep warm and use only as needed.

steps.title: Brown the butter
steps.text: Set the PossibleCooker to Sear/Sauté LOW with the lid off. Add {butter} and stir for 2–4 minutes until the milk solids are golden and smell nutty.

steps.title: Soften the mushrooms
steps.text: Add {mushrooms} with a splash of {broth} and stir for 3–5 minutes until soft and juicy.

steps.title: Simmer the barley
steps.text: Add {barley}, {thyme} and the remaining {broth}. Bring to a simmer on Sear/Sauté HIGH, then switch to LOW. Simmer uncovered for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the barley is tender and there is still a little creamy liquid. Add a splash of {topup} if the pot grows dry.

steps.title: Finish with hazelnut
steps.text: Turn the cooker off. Loosen {hazelnut} with a spoonful of the cooking liquid and stir back through the barley. Let stand 2 minutes, then spoon the moist pilaf alongside a sauced main.

notes: Make ahead: Mince the mushrooms up to a day ahead. Use quick-cooking barley for the stated timing. For dairy-free pilaf, skip the browning step and soften the mushrooms in avocado oil and broth; the hazelnut paste provides the nutty finish. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the soft pilaf in small portions for up to 6 weeks. Barley firms up in the freezer, so add a splash of broth on reheating. Fridge reheat: Warm a single portion with its sauce in a covered HexClad skillet over medium-low, adding a splash of water if thick. Stir or turn gently and begin checking after 5 minutes. Heat the barley to 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Use the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 272 kcal, 7.7 g protein, 41.0 g total carbohydrate, 9.6 g fat, 8.4 g fiber, 22 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
